root_causes.description: product-catalog, a leaf service with no downstream dependencies, exhibits a severe p99 latency spike (~9600ms with max exactly 10000ms) during the incident window. The hard 10-second ceiling on span durations combined with normal CPU usage (0.011 cores) indicates an injected/abnormal delay (e.g., network latency fault injection or blocking call) in product-catalog rather than resource exhaustion.

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage mean=0.011, p99=0.012, max=0.012, no anomaly detected
evidence.expected_baseline: cpu_usage < 0.1 cores; rules out cpu_stress as the cause of the latency
p99_latency_ms ~2ms; confirms fault is isolated to the product-catalog path, not cluster-wide

root_causes.description: checkout's p99 latency spiked to ~9400ms because it synchronously calls product-catalog (topology: checkout → cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog) and inherits the downstream 10s delay. Its other leaf dependencies (payment, shipping) remained fast, confirming propagation rather than a local fault.

evidence.observed_value: p99_latency_ms mean=1979.880, p95=7844.970, p99=9408.994, max=9800.000, anomaly detected

evidence.expected_baseline: p99_latency_ms ~2ms; checkout's other downstream dependencies are healthy

root_causes.description: frontend p99 latency reached ~9600ms (max 10000ms) as the user-facing aggregation of checkout and direct product-catalog/recommendation calls, all slowed by the product-catalog delay. recommendation also degraded (~4627ms p99) since it calls product-catalog, corroborating a single upstream origin.

evidence.observed_value: p99_latency_ms mean=2021.952, p95=8007.325, p99=9601.465, max=10000.000, anomaly detected
p99_latency_ms mean=967.976, p95=3856.994, p99=4627.399, max=4820.000, anomaly detected
evidence.expected_baseline: p99_latency_ms < 100ms; recommendation → product-catalog dependency explains partial degradation

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog for an injected delay fault (e.g., ChaosMesh NetworkChaos latency experiment, service-mesh fault injection, or a blocking sleep in a recent code/config change) and remove or roll it back; the exact 10000ms max span duration indicates a fixed 10s delay.
Restart or redeploy product-catalog pods in namespace otel-demo to clear any stuck/blocking state if the delay persists after removing the fault source.
Add strict timeouts (well below 10s) and circuit breakers on product-catalog calls from checkout, frontend, and recommendation so a single slow dependency cannot inflate end-user p99 to 10s.
Verify recovery by re-querying p99 latency for product-catalog, checkout, and frontend after remediation and confirm the anomaly window closes.
